name: SC-06
label: Safe D

key_factors: Clyburn's large fundraising and cash advantage
Prediction markets price near-certain Democratic win
model.rationale: Clyburn, a longtime incumbent in a D+13 district, holds a decisive money edge and markets price his reelection at roughly 96%, so fundamentals point firmly to a Safe Democratic hold.
model.watch: A major red-wave environment or an unexpected Clyburn stumble could narrow the margin, though a flip remains highly unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
South Carolina's 6th District, anchored in Columbia and Charleston's Democratic-leaning areas, has reelected Jim Clyburn repeatedly since 1993. The district's partisan lean of D+13 gives Republicans little structural opening, and Clyburn's national profile and seniority reinforce his standing.

Clyburn has raised over $1.2 million with $1.6 million on hand, while Republican John Peterson reports no fundraising figures. Prediction markets price a Democratic win at about 96 percent. With no public polling and no expert ratings, the race rests on fundamentals, all of which favor the incumbent comfortably.
